messages:
priya: Heads up — we hit a recurring egress tail spike on rack-3 (eu-west) during the 21:00 UTC window. Looks like a noisy tenant shadowing burst that cascades into the shared NIC queue. Trying to decide between a short-term egress throttle ladder and asking product/finance for a dedicated safety-net commit. Thoughts? :thinking:

alex: Can you paste the metric window and a link to traces?

priya: Pasted snippet below + link to waterfall (sent to channel).
```
egress_qps.rack-3: 1200 -> 4200 (peak)
nic_queue_len.p95: 3ms -> 85ms
kv_cache_miss.rate: 2% -> 18%
flow_retries: +1200
```

maria: Oof. That p95 jump screams queue saturation. Are these preemptible slice jobs or customer reserved slices?

priya: Mixed. Primary culprit looks like a single tenant running high-concurrency reranking on a warm pool that spilled into shared lanes. The allocator didn't spot the burst until egress hit TC.

sam: Short term we can enforce an egress-throttle ladder: tiered caps that step in at 60/80/95 percent of nic bandwidth with soft-backoff. Lowering concurrency at the proxy edge for offending slice would buy time.

julian: Agree. Also consider an aggressive KV-cache shielding rule: if a tenant's KV miss rate spikes >10% during a window, divert them to prewarmed dedicated lanes or apply a token bucket throttle. That keeps latency SLOs from regressing for others.

priya: Proposal sketch for ops play:
- 0-60% nic: no change
- 60-80% nic: soft throttle (10-20% concurrency reduction)
- 80-95% nic: hard throttle + reroute to preemptible warm pool
- >95% nic: emergency dedicate one warm-slice or preempt low-priority jobs
Would require scheduler + proxy change.

alex: What's the cost delta if we just reserve a small dedicated safety-net pool for top-tier customers? Finance wants numbers.

maria: Quick napkin: a 4-GPU dedicated warm-slice in eu-west at current cost adds ~"$3.2k/mo" (including infra & margin) but avoids 2-3 incidents/mo that cost ops time and potential SLA credits. If we carve that as an add-on, customers might accept it.

sam: We should also model tail risk: if two tenants spike simultaneously, dedicated 4-GPU won't fully absorb. Laddering plus a small dedicated carve is complementary.

priya: Ops impact question — how invasive is laddering on routing? Proxy can apply token buckets today per-tenant, but scheduler needs nic-level telemetry hooks to coordinate stepping. We can prototype with a probe + proxy-only mitigation for one week.

julian: I can throw together a quick BPF egress sensor that emits nic utilization + per-tenant qlen to telemetry. That would let us test ladder thresholds without scheduler changes.

infra-bot: deploy: canary rollout env=staging service=egress-proxy config=laddering-v1 by julian @ 1712234100

alex: Nice. After canary, run a 48h A/B: half-rack with laddering+proxy-only, half-rack baseline. Measure cross-tenant p99s and tail retries. If metrics look good, file a short RFC for scheduler hook.

maria: I'll run rough cost tradeoff with finance: ACL for dedicated-safety-net vs. ops time saved. Priya, pls collect incident minutes for last 3 months so we can quantify.

priya: On it. I'll upload the incident timeline + affected tenants. Expect that in ~2h.

sam: If prod needs immediate relief, low-friction temporary mitigation: reduce default max concurrency on warm pool ingress from 32 -> 24 for tenants without dedicated SLAs. It's crude but quick.

julian: Also flag: routing fallback must preserve model-compatibility. If we reroute to a quantized variant to reduce cost, customers might see quality changes. Need product sign-off.

priya: Noted. I'll coordinate with product on acceptable fallback model variants and include in the RFC.

alex: TL;DR action items: julian deploy probe & proxy ladder canary (in staging) -> priya gather incident minutes -> maria + finance cost model -> sam draft temporary concurrency tweak for prod rollback plan. I'll own the A/B analysis.

maria: Sounds good. :thumbsup:

priya: Thanks team. If laddering holds in canary, we can avoid asking customers for immediate dedicated add-ons and instead offer it as a premium for predictable latency.

alex: FYI tagging @product for fallback-model concern.

infra-bot: alert: egress-proxy laddering-v1 canary healthy after 20m (no regressions)

priya: Great — I'll post the incident summary when ready and kick off the RFC template.
